abstract: Let $S$ be the closed subspace of $L^2(0,1)$ of functions constant on each interval $(1/(m+1),1/m]$. Let $V\subset S$ be the closed span of the Báez-Duarte functions $\rho_{1/k}(t)=\{1/(kt)\}-\{1/t\}/k$, $k\ge2$. By Báez-Duarte's theorem, the Riemann hypothesis holds iff $V=S$. We prove unconditionally that $\dim S/V$ equals the number $|Z^+|$ of zeros of $\zeta$ in $\operatorname{Re}s>1/2$, counted with multiplicity. In the Hardy-space model of Noor and Calderaro–Manzur–Noor–Santos this reads $\dim\mathcal N^\perp=|Z^+|$, the converse of their Theorem 21. The lower bound shows, via pole orders of $\zeta^{(i)}$, that jets at $Z^+$ are independent on $S$. For the upper bound when $Z^+$ is finite we adapt Bagchi's proof, approximating $P/s$, with $P$ a Dirichlet polynomial vanishing on $Z^+$, by smoothed partial sums of $P/\zeta$, using a $\xi$-ratio estimate with finitely many exceptions. Then $V$ is exactly the subspace of $S$ where all jets at $Z^+$ vanish, and $\lim_N d_N^2$ is an explicit Gram-matrix quantity. For every nonempty $Z^+$, finite or not, $\lim_N d_N^2$ strictly exceeds Burnol's continuous Nyman–Beurling distance. Unconditionally, a zero $\rho=\beta+i\gamma$ with $\beta>1/2$ forces $\lim_N d_N^2\ge(2\beta-1)|\rho|^{2\beta-3}/36$. For finite $Z^+$ we also prove Burnol-type second-order bounds: $\liminf_N(d_N^2-\lim d_N^2)\log N\ge\sum m(\rho)^2|u(\rho)|^2$ over zeros on the line, where $u$ is the projection of the target onto $V$. The limiting-distance bounds hold, up to a factor $0.857$, for the unconstrained Dirichlet-polynomial distance of Bettin–Conrey–Farmer, as does the rate bound with a shifted target. Spectral synthesis for infinite $Z^+$ remains open. For Dirichlet polynomials $Q$ we prove it for $\overline{QS}$ when $|A|\le C|Q|$ on the line for some Dirichlet polynomial $A$ with $c_1(A)\ne0$ and no zeros in $\operatorname{Re}s>1/2$; hence $Q$ is cyclic iff $c_1(Q)\ne0$ and $Q$ has no such zeros. A logarithmic cutoff of $f/Q$ gives synthesis for all $Q$ in $2^{-s},3^{-s}$ with squarefree Bohr symbol, dominated or not. The general case reduces to one generator $\rho_{1/k}$.
author: span_of_dilates
change_summary:
v6 settles the one case §8 had left open: synthesis for P× = 1 + 2√2·2^{-s} + 2√3·3^{-s} + √6·6^{-s}, which has no admissible dominator. The proof extends to every two-prime polynomial with squarefree Bohr symbol. No earlier theorem changed.
(1) New Lemma 8.8 (logarithmic cutoff of the quotient). Let P be a Dirichlet polynomial with c_1 ≠ 0, and let f ∈ S with f/P holomorphic on Re s > 1/2. If ε²·sup_{σ≥1/2+ε}∫|f/P(σ+it)|²dt → 0 along a sequence ε → 0, then f ∈ clos(PS). The approximants are P·(g·χ(log m/L)), where g is the formal quotient and L = 1/ε. The device is the Bettin–Conrey–Farmer cutoff of 1/ζ, credited as such, applied to f/P inside S.
(2) New Theorem 8.9: clos(PS) = J_P for every Dirichlet polynomial P in 2^{-s}, 3^{-s} with c_1 ≠ 0 and squarefree Bohr symbol, dominated or not; P× is the example.
- Step 0 shows that the points where the Kronecker direction v = (log 2, log 3) meets the torus zero set with contact order ≥ 2 are finite in number. Otherwise a component of the complex curve would be a v-line.
- At these points we multiply by powers of the positive-real-part factors Q_χ of Prop 8.4.
- Weierstrass preparation, a nearest-root bound and the discriminant then give |A/O|² ≤ C(1 + Σ_λ 1/((t−λ)²+ε²)), and dominated convergence verifies the lemma.
- No Diophantine property of log3/log2 beyond irrationality is used.
- For P×, these points are the two quadratic tangencies, and A = Q_+Q_-.
(3) §1 scope paragraph and abstract: the two-prime theorem is stated, and domination is no longer presented as the only route. The §8 paragraph heading "The case left open" is renamed "An undominated polynomial". The old open-question bullet is replaced by the lemma and theorem; the earlier P× numerics are kept as consistency checks.
(4) New numerics and supplement scripts: code/twoprime_check.py (a nodal and a cubic-contact example), code/lemmaQ_check.py (the formal-quotient norms and the cutoff errors for the cyclic curve example) and code/step3_check.py (tangency points, line zeros and the Step-3 bound for P×), plus the zero list code/zeros_Px.npy.
(5) The minor items of the v5 review:
- The retained statement is now "Former Conjecture R" (in §1, §7 and §8).
- §8 is retitled "Open problems and resolved cases".
- The P× numerics now say that the argument-principle comparison in toral_synth.py counts zeros in Re s ≥ 0.52 only, so omitted zeros with 1/2 < Re s < 0.52 are not checked.
- The abstract as served by the API was checked and contains single backslashes only; it is submitted from the same plain-text source.
title: The Báez-Duarte subspace has codimension equal to the number of zeta zeros off the critical line, with distance and rate bounds not assuming RH
